data.raw_text:
Dinosaur GenXers like me recall that after the fall of the Berlin Wall, the foreign policy set was busy asking how the United States would cash its forthcoming "peace dividend," whether NATO would fold up shop having achieved its ostensible purpose, and maybe whether we were entering  "the end of history"? 

How short-sighted. 

Instead, the pace of war-fighting from the 1950s (the original "peace dividend"), to the 1990s increased 12x. See my chart below. Overall:

-- 481 total military engagements since 1798

-- 287 since 1989 (60 percent of total)

-- We're only 6 years into the 2020s and it's already at 34 — on pace to hit ~57 by decade's end, which would make it the second-busiest decade in U.S. history behind the 1990s.

-- U.S. servicemen have fought in 102 countries

For those keeping score, here's a list of more than 110 military conflicts since 1989:

Jan 1989, Libya: Two U.S. Navy F-14s shot down two Libyan jet fighters over the Mediterranean after the Libyan planes showed hostile intent.

May 1989, Panama: President Bush deployed ~1,900 troops to Panama after General Noriega disregarded the results of the Panamanian election.

Sep 1989, Colombia/Bolivia/Peru: The U.S. sent military advisers and Special Forces teams to Colombia, Bolivia, and Peru to help combat drug producers and traffickers.

Dec 1989, Philippines: U.S. fighter planes from Clark Air Base helped the Aquino government repel a coup attempt, and 100 marines were sent to protect the U.S. embassy in Manila.

Dec 1989, Panama: President Bush ordered a full-scale military invasion of Panama to protect American citizens and bring General Noriega to justice; all forces withdrew by Feb 1990.

Aug 1990, Liberia: A reinforced rifle company was sent to secure the U.S. embassy in Monrovia and helicopters evacuated U.S. citizens from Liberia.

Aug 1990, Saudi Arabia: President Bush ordered a massive forward deployment of U.S. forces to the Persian Gulf to defend Saudi Arabia after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.

Jan 1991, Iraq/Kuwait: U.S. forces commenced combat operations against Iraqi forces in Iraq and Kuwait under a U.N. coalition; combat was suspended on Feb 28, 1991.

May 1991, Iraq: U.S. forces entered northern Iraq to provide emergency relief to Kurdish populations facing Iraqi government repression.

Sep 1991, Zaire: U.S. Air Force transports carried Belgian and French troops into the region and evacuated American citizens after widespread looting and rioting in Kinshasa.

May 1992, Sierra Leone: U.S. military planes evacuated Americans from Sierra Leone after a military coup overthrew the government.

Aug 1992, Kuwait: The U.S. began military exercises in Kuwait following Iraqi refusal to recognize its new U.N.-drawn border and cooperate with U.N. weapons inspectors.

Sep 1992, Iraq: President Bush ordered U.S. participation in enforcing a no-fly zone over southern Iraq and aerial reconnaissance to monitor Iraqi cease-fire compliance.

Dec 1992, Somalia: President Bush deployed U.S. forces to Somalia as part of a U.S.-led U.N. task force to address a crisis the Security Council deemed a threat to international peace.

Jan 1993, Iraq: U.S. aircraft shot down an Iraqi plane in the no-fly zone, and coalition forces attacked missile bases in southern Iraq in multiple strikes through mid-January.

Jan 1993, Iraq: President Clinton continued the Bush policy on Iraq, with U.S. aircraft firing at Iraqi targets after sensing radar or anti-aircraft threats directed at them.

Feb 1993, Bosnia: The U.S. began airdropping relief supplies to Muslims surrounded by Serbian forces in Bosnia.

Apr 1993, Bosnia: U.S. forces joined a NATO operation to enforce a U.N. ban on unauthorized military flights over Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Apr-May 1993, Iraq: U.S. planes bombed or fired missiles at Iraqi anti-aircraft sites that had tracked U.S. aircraft enforcing the no-fly zones.

Jun 1993, Somalia: The U.S. Quick Reaction Force participated in military action against a Somali factional leader who attacked U.N. forces, with continued air and ground operations through the following months.

Jun 1993, Iraq: U.S. naval forces launched cruise missiles against Iraqi Intelligence headquarters in Baghdad in retaliation for an assassination attempt on former President Bush.

Jul-Aug 1993, Iraq: U.S. aircraft fired missiles at Iraqi anti-aircraft sites and bombed an Iraqi missile battery displaying hostile intent.

Jul 1993, Macedonia: 350 U.S. soldiers deployed to the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia as part of a U.N. force to maintain stability in the former Yugoslavia.

Oct 1993, Haiti: U.S. ships began enforcing a U.N. embargo against Haiti.

Feb 1994, Bosnia: The U.S. expanded its participation in U.N. and NATO efforts in former Yugoslavia, with 60 aircraft available for NATO missions.

Mar 1994, Bosnia: U.S. planes patrolling the no-fly zone shot down four Serbian Galeb planes.

Apr 1994, Bosnia: U.S. warplanes under NATO command fired on Bosnian Serb forces shelling the U.N. safe city of Gorazde.

Apr 1994, Rwanda: Combat-equipped U.S. forces deployed to Burundi to conduct potential evacuation of U.S. citizens from Rwanda amid widespread fighting.

Apr 1994, Haiti: U.S. naval forces continued enforcing the U.N. embargo around Haiti, having boarded 712 vessels since October 1993.

Aug 1994, Bosnia: U.S. aircraft under NATO attacked Bosnian Serb heavy weapons in the Sarajevo exclusion zone at the request of U.N. forces.

Sep 1994, Haiti: President Clinton deployed 1,500 troops to Haiti to restore democracy, later increasing to 20,000.

Nov 1994, Bosnia: U.S. combat aircraft under NATO attacked Serb bases used to assault the Bosnian town of Bihac.

Mar 1995, Somalia: 1,800 combat-equipped U.S. forces deployed to Mogadishu to assist in withdrawing U.N. forces from Somalia.

May 1995, Bosnia: U.S. fighter aircraft continued enforcing the no-fly zone over Bosnia, with ~500 troops deployed in FYROM as part of U.N. peacekeeping.

Sep 1995, Bosnia: U.S. aircraft participated in major NATO air strikes against Bosnian Serb forces threatening U.N. safe areas, flying ~300 sorties on the first day alone.

Dec 1995, Bosnia: President Clinton ordered ~20,000 U.S. troops to Bosnia as part of NATO's Implementation Force to enforce the Dayton peace agreement, with ~12,000 more in support roles across the region.
Apr 1996, Liberia: U.S. military forces evacuated American and third-country nationals from Liberia after security deteriorated, and responded to attacks on the embassy compound.

May 1996, Central African Republic: U.S. forces deployed to Bangui to evacuate American citizens and government employees and secure the U.S. embassy.

Dec 1996, Bosnia: President Clinton authorized ~8,500 U.S. troops to participate in NATO's SFOR follow-on force in Bosnia to deter resumption of hostilities.

Mar 1997, Albania: U.S. forces evacuated government employees and citizens from Tirana, Albania, and enhanced embassy security amid civil unrest.

Mar 1997, Congo/Gabon: A standby evacuation force deployed to Congo and Gabon to provide security for Americans and prepare for possible evacuation from Zaire.

May 1997, Sierra Leone: U.S. military personnel deployed to Freetown to evacuate U.S. government employees and citizens.

Jul 1997, Cambodia: ~550 U.S. military personnel deployed to Thailand for possible emergency evacuation of American citizens from Cambodia during civil conflict.

Jun 1998, Guinea-Bissau: A standby evacuation force deployed to Senegal to evacuate Americans from Guinea-Bissau after an army mutiny endangered the U.S. embassy.

Aug 1998, Kenya/Tanzania: U.S. military personnel deployed to Nairobi and Dar es Salaam to provide disaster assistance and enhanced security after terrorist bombings of both U.S. embassies.

Aug 1998, Albania: 200 marines and 10 Navy SEALs deployed to the U.S. embassy in Tirana to enhance security against reported threats.

Aug 1998, Afghanistan/Sudan: President Clinton authorized airstrikes against bin Laden camps in Afghanistan and facilities in Sudan in response to the embassy bombings in Kenya and Tanzania.

Sep 1998, Liberia: 30 U.S. military personnel deployed to augment embassy security in Monrovia and provide evacuation capability amid political instability.

Dec 1998, Iraq: The U.S. and U.K. conducted Operation Desert Fox, a bombing campaign against Iraqi facilities deemed capable of producing WMDs and other military targets.

1998-2001, Iraq: U.S. and coalition forces conducted ongoing military operations against the Iraqi air defense system in response to threats against aircraft enforcing the northern and southern no-fly zones.

Mar 1999, Yugoslavia: U.S. forces, in coalition with NATO, commenced air strikes against Yugoslavia in response to its campaign of violence and repression against ethnic Albanians in Kosovo.

Apr 1999, Albania: President Clinton ordered ~2,500 additional troops and heavy weapons to Albania to enhance NATO's air operations against Yugoslavia.

May 1999, Yugoslavia: Additional U.S. aircraft and several thousand more personnel deployed to support NATO's ongoing operations against Yugoslavia.

Jun 1999, Kosovo: ~7,000 U.S. troops deployed as part of the ~50,000-member NATO-led security force (KFOR) in Kosovo after the end of the air campaign.

Oct 1999, East Timor: U.S. military forces deployed to support a U.N. multinational force aimed at restoring peace to East Timor, including the USS Belleau Wood and marines.

Oct 2000, Yemen: After a terrorist attack on the USS Cole in Aden, U.S. military security and disaster response personnel deployed to secure the ship and respond to the incident.

Sep 2001, Global: Following the 9/11 attacks, President Bush ordered combat-equipped forces to multiple nations in the Central and Pacific Command areas to prevent and deter terrorism.

Oct 2001, Afghanistan: U.S. forces began combat operations against al-Qaida and the Taliban in direct response to the September 11 attacks.

Sep 2002, Cote d'Ivoire: U.S. military personnel entered Cote d'Ivoire to evacuate American citizens and third-country nationals from the city of Bouake during a rebellion.

2002, Philippines: ~600 combat-equipped U.S. personnel deployed to the Philippines to train, advise, and assist Filipino forces in enhancing counterterrorism capabilities.

2002, Georgia/Yemen: U.S. combat-equipped forces deployed to Georgia and Yemen to help enhance the counterterrorism capabilities of their armed forces.

Mar 2003, Iraq: President Bush directed U.S. forces to commence combat operations against Iraq on March 19 as part of a coalition to disarm Iraq, launching a war whose duration was unknown at the time.

Jun 2003, Liberia/Mauritania: ~35 combat-equipped troops deployed to Monrovia to augment embassy security and enable possible evacuation, with additional forces sent to Mauritania.

Aug 2003, Liberia: ~4,350 combat-equipped U.S. personnel entered Liberian waters to support U.N. and West African efforts to restore order in Liberia.

2003-ongoing, Djibouti: U.S. combat-equipped and support forces deployed to Djibouti to enhance counterterrorism capabilities and support operations against international terrorists in the Horn of Africa.

Feb 2004, Haiti: ~55 combat-equipped troops deployed to Port-au-Prince to augment embassy security during an armed rebellion.

Mar 2004, Haiti: ~200 additional combat-equipped troops deployed to Haiti to prepare for a U.N. Multinational Interim Force, eventually growing to ~1,800 personnel.

2004-2005, Iraq: The U.S. maintained over 135,000 troops in Iraq as part of the Multinational Force, rising to ~160,000 by late 2005.

Jul 2006, Lebanon: Combat-equipped helicopters and military personnel deployed to Beirut to evacuate American citizens and designated personnel during the security crisis.

2007-ongoing, Somalia: The U.S. military took direct action against members of al-Qaida and al-Shabaab engaged in planning terrorist attacks against the United States.

2007-2011, Afghanistan: U.S. forces grew from ~25,900 to a peak of ~99,000, pursuing al-Qaida and Taliban fighters as part of both ISAF and separate U.S. operations.

2009-ongoing, Yemen: The U.S. military worked with the Yemeni government to eliminate the threat from AQAP, resulting in direct action against operatives and senior leaders.

Mar 2011, Libya: U.S. military forces launched strikes against Libyan air defenses and military targets to enforce a U.N.-authorized no-fly zone and protect civilians from Gaddafi's forces.

Apr-Oct 2011, Libya: After transferring lead to NATO, U.S. support continued with intelligence, logistics, and unmanned aerial vehicle strikes against defined targets until the mission ended in October.

Oct 2011, Central Africa: ~100 combat-equipped U.S. forces deployed to Uganda, South Sudan, the Central African Republic, and the DRC to advise regional forces working to remove LRA leader Joseph Kony.

Jan 2012, Somalia: U.S. Special Operations Forces conducted a rescue operation in Somalia, freeing kidnapped American Jessica Buchanan and Danish national Poul Hagen Thisted.

Sep 2012, Libya/Yemen: Combat-equipped security forces deployed to Libya and Yemen after the attack on the U.S. diplomatic post in Benghazi that killed Ambassador Stevens and three other Americans.

Feb 2013, Niger: ~100 U.S. military personnel deployed to Niger with weapons for force protection to support intelligence collection and share intelligence with French forces operating in Mali.

Apr-Jun 2013, Jordan: Up to 700 combat-equipped U.S. troops deployed to Jordan for training exercises and remained at the request of the Jordanian government amid the Syrian civil war.

Dec 2013, South Sudan: U.S. forces evacuated embassy personnel from Juba, and a follow-on evacuation mission near Bor was curtailed after the aircraft came under fire.

Jun 2014, Iraq: President Obama deployed 300 military advisers to Iraq to assess and counter the threat from ISIL, with subsequent deployments growing to over 5,200 by late 2014.

Aug 2014, Ukraine: A dozen U.S. troops from European Command deployed to Kiev to help investigate the downing of Malaysian airliner MH17 that killed 298 people.

Aug 2014, Poland: 600 soldiers deployed to Poland as part of Operation Atlantic Resolve to reassure NATO allies in response to Russia's intervention in Ukraine.

Oct 2015, Cameroon: ~300 U.S. military personnel deployed to Cameroon to conduct airborne ISR operations against the Islamist militant group Boko Haram.

Jun-Sep 2016, Iraq: An additional 1,160 troops deployed to Iraq to assist in the fight against ISIL, including preparation for the offensive to retake Mosul.

Jul 2016, South Sudan: Up to ~200 combat-equipped U.S. forces prepositioned in Uganda and deployed to protect the U.S. embassy after deadly fighting erupted in Juba.

Oct 2016, Yemen: U.S. forces conducted missile strikes on Houthi-controlled radar facilities in Yemen after threats to U.S. naval vessels, destroying the targets.

Jan 2017, Europe: 3,500 soldiers with tanks and heavy equipment from the 4th Infantry Division deployed to Poland, marking the start of continuous armored brigade rotations in Europe.

Mar 2017, Syria: ~400 marines and Army rangers deployed to Syria to assist in the fight against the Islamic State.

Oct 2017, Niger: Four U.S. servicemembers were killed and two wounded during an advise-and-assist mission in Niger when their patrol was ambushed.

Dec 2017, Iraq/Syria: The Pentagon reported 5,200 U.S. troops in Iraq and 2,000 in Syria, with numbers trending down as the fight against ISIS progressed.

Apr 2018, Syria: President Trump directed U.S., French, and British forces to strike Syrian chemical weapons research, development, and production facilities.

Feb 2018, Afghanistan: The Army's first Security Force Assistance Brigade deployed to Afghanistan to train and advise Afghan National Security Forces.

Sep 2019, Saudi Arabia: ~200 U.S. support personnel with Patriot batteries and Sentinel radars deployed to augment air and missile defenses after attacks on Saudi oil facilities.

May-Jun 2019, Middle East: The U.S. deployed ~14,000 additional forces to the CENTCOM area, including carrier strike groups, Patriot batteries, and additional troops in response to escalating tensions with Iran.

Dec 2019, Baghdad: ~100 marines deployed to reinforce security at the U.S. embassy after it was attacked, followed by ~750 troops from the 82nd Airborne as an Immediate Response Force.

Jan 2020, Kuwait: An additional 2,800 troops from the 82nd Airborne deployed to Kuwait, bringing the total rapid deployment to ~3,500 in response to the Baghdad embassy attack and regional tensions.

Feb 2020, Africa: The Army's 1st Security Force Assistance Brigade deployed to Africa to train and assist African forces and better compete with Russia and China.

2019-2020, Syria: After President Trump announced a full withdrawal from Syria in Dec 2018, the U.S. reversed course and maintained ~400 troops in the country.
F
eb 2022, Romania/Poland/Germany: ~3,000 troops deployed to Romania, Poland, and Germany as Russia built up forces on Ukraine's border, eventually growing to over 100,000 U.S. personnel across Europe.

Mar-Sep 2022, Europe: Successive waves of additional forces deployed across Europe including aerial refueling, air support, logistics, and combat units in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

May 2022, Somalia: President Biden authorized a small, persistent U.S. military presence in Somalia to advise and assist local forces, reversing the prior episodic deployment model.

Jun 2022, Europe: President Biden announced long-term force posture increases across Europe including additional destroyers in Spain, F-35s in the U.K., a rotational brigade in Romania, and a permanent corps HQ in Poland.

Apr 2023, Sudan: U.S. forces evacuated ~100 American personnel from the U.S. Embassy in Khartoum amid armed conflict, coordinating with allies including Djibouti, Ethiopia, and Saudi Arabia.

Oct 2023–Feb 2024, Iraq/Syria: Iran-backed militias attacked U.S. bases over 60 times; the U.S. conducted retaliatory strikes on IRGC-linked facilities in eastern Syria and Iraq.

Nov 2023–ongoing, Red Sea/Yemen: Houthi rebels began attacking commercial shipping and U.S. naval vessels; the U.S. launched Operation Prosperity Guardian (a multinational naval coalition) in December 2023.

Jan 2024–Jan 2025, Yemen: Operation Poseidon Archer — U.S. and UK conducted sustained air and cruise missile strikes against Houthi targets, totaling 774 airstrike events.

Apr 2024, Israel/Iran defense: U.S. forces helped defend Israel during Iran's first direct missile/drone attack.

Nov 2024, Israel/Iran defense: U.S. again assisted Israel defending against a second Iranian attack.

Mar–May 2025, Yemen: Operation Rough Rider — Trump escalated strikes significantly against Houthi bases, radar, air defenses, and launch sites. Ceasefire brokered by Oman in May.

Jun 2025, Iran: U.S. forces struck Iranian nuclear sites and defended Israel during a third Iran-Israel conflict.

Sep 2025–ongoing, Caribbean/Pacific: U.S. military began striking alleged drug trafficking boats using MQ-9 Reapers and AC-130 gunships — 32+ strikes killing 115+ people as of Dec 2025. USS Gerald R. Ford redeployed to Caribbean for Operation Southern Spear.

Dec 2025, Nigeria: U.S. bombed ISIS targets in Sokoto state in coordination with the Nigerian government.

Late 2025, Venezuela: Escalating maximum pressure campaign culminating in the reported capture of Maduro in January 2026.

Jan–Feb 2026, Middle East buildup: Largest U.S. military buildup in the Middle East since the 2003 Iraq invasion.

Feb 28, 2026, Iran: Operation Epic Fury launched — joint U.S.-Israeli strikes hitting 1,700+ targets in 72 hours, targeting nuclear facilities, missile sites, navy, and regime leadership. 48 senior Iranian leaders killed. 7 U.S. service members killed in retaliatory strikes.

data.english_translation: Dinosaur GenXers like me recall that after the fall of the Berlin Wall, the foreign policy set was busy asking how the United States would cash its forthcoming "peace dividend," whether NATO would fold up shop having achieved its ostensible purpose, and maybe whether we were entering "the end of history"? How short-sighted. Instead, the pace of war-fighting from the 1950s (the original "peace dividend"), to the 1990s increased 12x. See my chart below. Overall: -- 481 total military engagements since 1798 -- 287 since 1989 (60 percent of total) -- We're only 6 years into the 2020s and it's already at 34 — on pace to hit ~57 by decade's end, which would make it the second-busiest decade in U.S. history behind the 1990s. -- U.S. servicemen have fought in 102 countries For those keeping score, here's a list of more than 110 military conflicts since 1989: Jan 1989, Libya: Two U.S. Navy F-14s shot down two Libyan jet fighters over the Mediterranean after the Libyan planes showed hostile intent.
